items.prompt: Choose the pronoun for Mia. '___ likes to draw.'
hints: Mia is a girl.
A pronoun takes the place of a name.
Which word do we use for one girl?
items.explanation: Mia is a girl, so we use she: She likes to draw.

options.why: He is for a boy or a man.
It is for a thing or an animal.
They is for more than one.

items.prompt: Choose the pronoun. 'Tom and Ali are friends. ___ play football.'
hints: Count the people.
Tom and Ali are two people.
Which pronoun is for more than one?
items.explanation: Tom and Ali are two people, so we use they.

options.why: He is for one boy.
She is for one girl.
It is for a thing.

items.prompt: Choose the pronoun. 'The cat is hungry. ___ wants some fish.'
hints: The cat is an animal.
We can use the same word for an animal or a thing.
Is the cat one animal or more?
items.explanation: We can use it for an animal: It wants some fish.

options.why: They is for more than one.
We means me and other people.
I means the person speaking.

items.prompt: Match each name to a pronoun.
hints: Think about who or what each one is.
He is for a boy or man. She is for a girl or woman.
Start with the bike. Is it a person?
items.explanation: Grandpa is he, Aunt Rosa is she, the bike is it, and Dina and Rio are they.

items.prompt: Write the pronoun. 'My friends and I like rice. ___ eat it every day.'
hints: My friends and I means more than one person.
You are one of the people.
Which pronoun means me and others?
items.explanation: My friends and I includes you, so we use we: We eat it every day.

items.prompt: Sort the pronouns. One person or more than one?
hints: Think how many people each word means.
We and us include you and other people.
Start with they. Is it one person or more?
items.explanation: He, she and I mean one person. They, we and us mean more than one.

items.prompt: Which word can replace 'the boys'? 'I saw the boys at the park.'
hints: There is more than one boy.
The boys come after the doing word saw.
Try each word: I saw ___ at the park.
items.explanation: After a doing word, we use them for more than one: I saw them at the park.

options.why: They goes before a doing word, like they play. After saw, we use them.
Him is for one boy.
Us includes you.

items.prompt: Choose the missing word. 'Lina has a red bag. ___ bag is new.'
hints: The bag belongs to Lina.
We need a word that shows whose bag it is.
Lina is a girl. Whose bag is it?
items.explanation: Her shows the bag belongs to Lina: Her bag is new.

options.why: She does the action. Here we need a word that shows whose bag.
His is for a boy.
It does not show whose bag it is.

items.prompt: Choose all the pronouns. 'She gave it to me.'
hints: Three words are pronouns.
Pronouns stand in for people and things.
Which words could be swapped for a name or a thing?
items.explanation: She, it and me are pronouns. They take the place of names and things.

options.why: Gave is a doing word.
To is a small linking word.

items.prompt: Change the name to a pronoun. 'Dad is cooking. ___ is making soup.'
hints: Dad is a man.
We use a pronoun so we do not say Dad again.
Which pronoun is for one man?
items.explanation: Dad is a man, so we use he: He is making soup.

items.prompt: Choose the correct sentence.
hints: Take Ali away. Which sounds right: I went, or me went?
Polite speakers name the other person first.
Find the sentence that does both.
items.explanation: We say I went, and we put the other person first: Ali and I went to the shop.

options.text: Me and Ali went to the shop.
options.why: Me does not start a sentence like this.

options.text: Ali and I went to the shop.
Ali and me went to the shop.
options.why: Before went, we use I, not me.

options.text: I and Ali went to the shop.
options.why: It is polite to name the other person first.

items.prompt: Read: 'Pak Budi and his dog walk to the river. Then they sit by the water.' Who does they mean?
hints: They means more than one.
Who walks to the river?
Look back at the first sentence.
items.explanation: They means Pak Budi and his dog. They walk to the river, and then they sit down.

options.why: A river cannot sit.
Water cannot sit.
They means more than one.

items.prompt: Write a pronoun. 'Can you help ___? I cannot reach the shelf.'
hints: The person speaking needs help.
Read the second sentence: I cannot reach.
After help, we do not use I. What do we use?
items.explanation: The speaker needs help, so the pronoun is me: Can you help me?

items.prompt: Which sentence sounds best?
hints: Pronouns help us not to repeat names.
Check that each pronoun fits the person or thing.
The hat is a thing. Which pronoun is for a thing?
items.explanation: Her, she and it replace Dewi and the hat, so the sentence does not repeat words.

options.text: Dewi lost Dewi's hat, so Dewi looked for Dewi's hat.
options.why: Saying Dewi again and again sounds odd.

options.text: Dewi lost her hat, so she looked for it.
She lost her hat, so she looked for her.
options.why: The hat is a thing, so we use it, not her.

options.text: Dewi lost it hat, so it looked for her.
options.why: It is for things, not people.

items.prompt: How many pronouns are in this sentence? 'We gave him the ball, and he kicked it to them.'
hints: Pronouns take the place of names and things.
Find words like we, he and it.
Point to each pronoun as you count.
items.explanation: We, him, he, it and them are pronouns. That makes 5.

options.why: Count them all again.
Look at the end of the sentence.
Ball and gave are not pronouns.

items.prompt: Which pronouns are missing? 'Our class has a goldfish. ___ is orange. ___ feed it every morning.'
hints: The first gap is about the goldfish.
The second gap is about our class.
Our class includes you.
items.explanation: The goldfish is it, and our class is we: It is orange. We feed it every morning.

options.why: The goldfish is an animal, and our class includes us.
Us does not start a sentence like this.
There is only one goldfish.

items.prompt: Which word is a pronoun?
hints: A pronoun takes the place of a name.
It could replace Tom and Ali.
Which word could start: ___ are friends?
items.explanation: They is a pronoun. It can take the place of names.

options.why: Table is a noun.
Jump is a verb.
Green is an adjective.

items.prompt: Put the words in order to make a sentence.
hints: Start with the word that has a capital letter.
The sentence is about you and your friends.
It ends with the place where you learn.
items.explanation: We love our school. We and our are pronouns that show it is about us.

items.prompt: Ana is my sister. ___ is seven years old.
hints: A pronoun takes the place of a name.
Ana is a girl.
Which pronoun is for a girl?
items.explanation: Ana is a girl, so we use the pronoun she.

items.prompt: Which word can take the place of Sam? ___ is six.
hints: Sam is a boy.
We use a short word instead of the name.
It starts with H.
items.explanation: He takes the place of Sam.

options.why: Sam is a boy, so we use he.
It is for things and animals.
They is for more than one.

items.prompt: Which word can take the place of the girls?
hints: There is more than one girl.
We need a word for many.
It starts with Th.
items.explanation: They takes the place of the girls.

options.why: He is for one boy.
She is for one girl.
It is for one thing.

items.prompt: Mum has a bag. ___ is red.
hints: A bag is a thing.
There is one bag.
Use the short word for one thing.
items.explanation: It takes the place of the bag.

options.why: A bag is not a person.
A bag is not a person.
There is only one bag.

items.prompt: Tom and I are friends. ___ play together.
hints: Tom and I means the speaker is included.
There are two people.
The word starts with W.
items.explanation: We means Tom and I.

options.why: They does not include the speaker.
You is for the person you talk to.
He is for one boy.

items.prompt: Dina lost ___ book.
hints: Dina is a girl.
The book belongs to her.
Choose the word for a girl.
items.explanation: Her shows the book belongs to Dina.

items.prompt: Write the pronoun. The dogs run. ___ are fast.
hints: There is more than one dog.
Use a short word for many.
It starts with Th.
items.explanation: They takes the place of the dogs.

items.prompt: Sort the pronouns.
hints: Think about how many each word means.
He is one boy.
They is many.
items.explanation: He, she and it are one. They, we and them are more than one.

items.prompt: Match each name to its pronoun.
hints: Think about who or what.
A boy is he.
Two people are they.
items.explanation: Each pronoun takes the place of the noun.

items.prompt: Put the words in order to make a sentence.
hints: The sentence starts with a capital.
It ends with a full stop.
Me is near the end.
items.explanation: She gave it to me.

items.prompt: Which sentence is right?
hints: Try the sentence with I alone.
I went to the shop is right.
Put Sita next to I.
items.explanation: Sita and I went to the shop.

options.text: Me and Sita went to the shop.
options.why: Use I when you do the action.

options.text: Sita and me went to the shop.
options.why: Use I when you do the action.
Us cannot start the sentence.

options.text: Sita and I went to the shop.

items.prompt: Choose all the pronouns.
hints: Pronouns take the place of names.
Two choices are pronouns.
They are short words.
items.explanation: She and they are pronouns.

options.why: Run is a doing word.
Sita is a name.
Happy is a describing word.

items.prompt: Which word fits? The cat licked ___ paws.
hints: The paws belong to the cat.
It is one animal.
It has no apostrophe.
items.explanation: Its shows the paws belong to the cat.

options.why: It's means it is.
Their is for more than one.
Her is for a girl.
